## Packages

The analysis uses the [{tidyverse}](https://www.tidyverse.org/) for data handling. **[{usRds}](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/usRds/)** is the access package for the USRDS files: it locates the files on the machine that holds them and loads or extracts from them. The [coverage assessment](usrds-coverage.qmd) records which steps it does. **[{flowchart}](https://bruigtp.github.io/flowchart/)** builds the cohort flow diagram (Figure 1), **[{survival}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survival)** the Kaplan–Meier curve (Figure 2), and **[{labelled}](https://larmarange.github.io/labelled/)** the variable labels.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| eval: false
```

## Constants

These are the study's fixed parameters, each tied to the section of the [analysis plan](analysis-plan.qmd) that sets it:

- the admission window for the index hospitalization, 2006–2016 (§3);
- the age range, 18 to 90 years inclusive (§4);
- the 180-day mortality window, in which a death on day 180 counts (§7);
- the ICD-10 transition date (§5);
- the 2-year cut-off for time since transplant in the model (§5).

Scripts use these names rather than typing the numbers again.

#| eval: false

## Hospitalization file columns

The two USRDS hospitalization files store diagnoses differently, according to Appendix B of the Researcher's Guide (2024):

- **`hosp_to2009`** holds up to 10 diagnosis codes, in `HSDIAG1`–`HSDIAG10`. Its `PRIMDIAG` is only a yes/no flag saying whether the first diagnosis is the principal one.
- **`hosp_2010on`** holds the principal diagnosis code in `PRIMDIAG` and up to 26 more in `HSDIAG1`–`HSDIAG26`.

These constants name the columns that hold codes in each file, so a search never treats the old yes/no flag as a code.

```{r}
#| label: define-hospitalization-columns
#| eval: false
```

## UNOS keys and covariate concepts

The UNOS files link to one another by identifiers whose names changed between USRDS releases: the 2024 release adds `_CODE` to each. The registration key here, `TRR_ID`, is the one the reconstruction used with this project's release. The follow-up key, `TRRFU_ID`, has not been checked against that release.

**Decision pending:** the follow-up key name has to be confirmed against Appendix B for the release in use before the covariates script is run.

The concept lists name which diagnoses and procedures are flagged on the index stay.

```{r}
#| label: define-unos-keys
#| eval: false
```

## Outcome and model settings

These settings control the outcomes and models:

- **The end of death data for the USRDS release in use.** It is set by whoever runs the analysis, because the paper doesn't give it and it varies by release.
- **The age cut-off of 60** that the paper's model uses.
- **The P value for backward elimination.**
- **The list of candidate variables:** every characteristic in Tables 1 and 2, in the form the paper reports them.
- **The paper's final model:** its eight variables, with the adjusted odds ratios and confidence intervals it reports, for the comparison in Table 4.

**Decision pending:** `death_data_end_date` has to be set for the release in use; the outcomes script stops until it is.
